lines.text: You don’t usually think about this while you’re just living life, but a lot changes when you grow up, things you grew up with silently disappear and you don’t even notice.
Clothes stop fitting, but you don’t even notice.
Vegetables suddenly don’t seem like the worst thing in the world, but you don’t even notice.
People you knew as a kid that were older, grew up into adults way before you could, but you don’t even notice.
People grow up, and they move on with their lives…but you don’t even notice.

Except I did notice, I noticed immediately, nobody else seemed to, but I did, and I stayed quiet…because everyone seems to be “used to life”, like they’ve had lives before this one, everything naturally flows into place, things just change and no one bats an eye.
Bringing up the change just interrupts the flow of it all, it makes people aware.
And I learned…that people hate being aware.
I’m forced to live with being aware and not being able to talk about it with anybody.
Everyone around me just wants to act like change isn’t there, it really changed my perspective on how nostalgia makes me feel.
Nostalgia’s supposed to feel good, but everytime I get nostalgia I just get depressed.
I wish time would slow down.
But it doesn’t matter how I feel, life keeps moving…with or without you…whether you’re ready or not, that’s just the sad truth.
